searchText: I know, but I took the liberty to depict each field as an SSZ field, and not as its encoded version. And I understand that the transport protocol can provide framing, what I have said is tools (such as a wallet) outside of the transport protocol today can validate that the transaction is not truncated without recovering and validating the signature. This will be only possible with recovering the signature after this change. I'm not arguing for or against that, just noticed that is the case 🙂 Are there people who are receiving transactions over some protocol that doesn't give strong guarantees about completeness? Of such people, how many of them are not validating the data received? I think I see the point you are making, but I suspect that it probably doesn't matter. To clarify: I am really not making arguments against SSZ. This is just an observation. Not sure why things are always perceived as argumentation in this space 🤷‍♂️ No need to argue against SSZ, I have already done it (see <#745077610685661265>). 😬
